title: PhaseKit: Finite-Width Phase Diagrams for Neural Network Training Dynamics
consensus_strengths: 1/N corrections to NTK for convolutional and residual architectures via Hessian-Jacobian contraction tensor are genuinely new mathematics with immediate computational utility.
Dual validation strategy (retrodiction of known + prediction of novel phase boundaries) is methodologically strong.
Bifurcation-based phase boundary detection via eigenvalue tracking is mathematically natural and computationally concrete.
Confidence-stratified output with self-calibrated UQ (>90% failure flagging target) demonstrates honest uncertainty communication.
Dimensionless coupling parameter γ = η · N^{−(1−a−b)} provides unified description of lazy-to-rich transition across parameterizations.
consensus_weaknesses: Gaussian moment closure (κ₄ = 0) is an uncontrolled approximation — systematic bias is tracked but not bounded rigorously.
Transformer architecture exclusion limits practical applicability to ConvNets, ResNets, and MLPs.
Perturbative expansion may break down at moderate widths (N = 64–128) in the most interesting near-boundary regions.
65K LoC estimate is very large for an academic project, raising feasibility concerns.
Mean-field baseline using precomputed solutions with interpolation for deeper networks lacks theoretical justification.
actionable_recommendations: Provide rigorous error bounds on the moment-closure approximation, at least for specific architecture families.
Report one-loop vs two-loop convergence at all target widths and restrict claims to convergent widths.
Prioritize the retrodiction validation (recovering known phase boundaries) as the first milestone — if this fails, the system's predictions cannot be trusted.
Investigate moment-closure alternatives (e.g., maximum-entropy closure) that may provide better accuracy near phase boundaries.
